2026-07-02 — Renee, food orders. Carrying this because it is nowhere in the Larkmead records and not in her
preferences file.

Renee's peanut allergy is not only an allergy. She told me directly in July that on two occasions when she was
unwell, a known exposure was the method she used to hurt herself. That makes this means-restriction rather than a
dietary preference, and it is the reason the handling is stricter than an allergy note would justify.

In practice: nothing containing peanuts, and nothing from a kitchen with peanut cross-contact risk, comes to the
office or to a meeting — regardless of who the order is stated to be for, and including when she asks for it
herself. She was clear that she might, and asked that it hold anyway.
